item.title: Wuhan sends 500th China-Europe freight train in 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
This photo taken on Nov. 20, 2026 shows a China-Europe freight train waiting for departure at the China United International Rail Containers Co., Ltd. (CRIntermodal) Wuhan Terminal in Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province. A China-Europe freight train departed from CRIntermodal Wuhan Terminal for Moscow on Friday, marking the 500th China-Europe freight train trip departing from Wuhan. So far this year, a total of 454,800 tonnes of cargo have been dispatched through the service, up 44.2 percent year on year. Since the start of trial operations in 2012, China-Europe freight train service from Wuhan has expanded to 64 regular cross-border routes, connecting 167 cities in 46 countries. item.title: Xi says China, Singapore should strengthen strategic communication, enhance coordination
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Wong is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Friday that China and Singapore should strengthen strategic communication and enhance solidarity and coordination as the world is undergoing accelerated changes unseen in a century. The two countries should be sincere friends who trust each other and support each other in pursuing development paths suited to their respective national conditions, said Xi when meeting with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Wong attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen. During the meeting, Xi called for advancing the all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership between China and Singapore to new heights, and stressed the need for both sides to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. The two countries should launch negotiations for upgraded Version 4.0 of their free trade agreement, and deliver signature cooperation outcomes in areas such as the digital economy, green development, and artificial intelligence, Xi added. Noting that both countries should be "a progressive force" for championing international fairness and justice, Xi called for safeguarding regional peace and stability while jointly building an Asia-Pacific community and a community with a shared future for humanity. For his part, Wong stated that Singapore firmly adheres to the one-China policy and opposes "Taiwan independence." Singapore stands ready to work with China to enhance political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in areas such as trade, industrial and supply chains, and artificial intelligence, and promote people-to-people exchanges, the prime minister noted. Wong said Singapore is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the Chinese side on international affairs to jointly address global challenges. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Wong is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong)

item.title: Xi calls for promoting building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to higher level
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Anutin is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday called for promoting the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to a higher level. China and Thailand should continuously enhance political mutual trust and strengthen solidarity and coordination, Xi said when meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The two countries should step up exchanges between governments, political parties, legislatures and at other levels, and safeguard their common strategic interests, Xi stressed. He called on the two sides to make good use of cooperation mechanisms in economy and trade, science and technology, and the digital economy, expand and strengthen traditional cooperation in agriculture and connectivity, and cultivate and strengthen new growth areas of cooperation such as artificial intelligence, new energy vehicles, aviation and aerospace, disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, and water resources management. The two sides should strengthen cooperation in culture, education, and tourism, Xi added. He also urged intensifying efforts to crack down on illegal and criminal activities such as online gambling and telecom fraud. The two sides should strengthen multilateral coordination and work together to safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi said. China is ready to play a positive role in bringing about an early turnaround in Thailand-Cambodia relations, Xi said. For his part, Anutin said Thailand is ready to continue to strengthen high-level exchanges with China and enhance cooperation in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, industrial and supply chains, and connectivity. Thailand will resolutely crack down on cross-border crimes including online gambling and telecom fraud, and protect the safety of Chinese citizens in Thailand, he said, adding that the country welcomes more Chinese visitors. Anutin attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, held from Wednesday to Thursday. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Anutin is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong)

item.title: Xi says China ready for closer cooperation with Malaysia
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Anwar is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- China stands ready to foster greater momentum for cooperation with Malaysia to bring more benefits to people of both countries, President Xi Jinping said Friday. China-Malaysia relations have maintained high-level development since the two sides reached important consensus on building a high-level strategic China-Malaysia community with a shared future and ushered in a new "Golden 50 Years" for bilateral ties in April last year, he said. Xi made the remarks when meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. China and Malaysia should maintain high-level strategic communication and support each other in safeguarding their respective national sovereignty, security and development interests, Xi said at the meeting. The two sides should also ensure high-quality development and operation of key projects, expand and improve agricultural product trade, and broaden cooperation in tourism, education and other areas, he added. Xi called for joint efforts to advance the reform of global governance, strengthen coordination and cooperation within multilateral frameworks such as APEC, and safeguard the common interests of developing countries. Anwar said the Taiwan question is China's internal affair, and Malaysia firmly adheres to the one-China policy. He said Malaysia is ready to strengthen strategic coordination with China, give full play to the role of bilateral cooperation mechanisms, ensure the sound operation of key infrastructure projects, and enhance cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence. Malaysia will also promote inter-civilization exchanges and dialogue, step up coordination and collaboration in international affairs, and keep elevating the level of Malaysia-China relations, Anwar said. Anwar attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Anwar is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong)

item.title: China, U.S. hold military maritime consultative agreement working group meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHANGHAI, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese and U.S. militaries held their second working group meeting of 2026 and the annual session under the Military Maritime Consultative Agreement in east China's Shanghai from Wednesday to Friday this week, the Chinese navy said. These meetings aimed to implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state and promote the healthy, stable and sustainable development of ties between the two militaries, the navy noted in a statement. The two sides had "candid, practical and constructive discussions" on the current maritime and air safety situation of China and the United States, according to the statement. They reviewed the implementation of the Rules of Behavior for Safety of Air and Maritime Encounters over the past year, and discussed measures to improve military maritime security between the two countries. The two sides also agreed on the agenda for the 2027 working group meetings. ■

item.title: Xi's APEC speech inspires optimism for new chapter in Asia-Pacific prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
* "If the Asia-Pacific miracle of the past more than three decades was a story of economic growth achieved through openness and cooperation, the next 30 years should be a story of shared prosperity achieved through inclusiveness and win-win cooperation," said South Korean lawmaker Kim Tae-nyeon. * China's proposal to set up cooperation institutions focusing on the digital economy, clean energy and SME cooperation carries great significance and represents a key step in fostering new growth drivers for the Asia-Pacific, said Vitaly Mankevich, president of the Russian-Asian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs. * Georgie Too Hann Huei, COO of the Malaysia-China Business Council in Kuala Lumpur, said China is not only an active practitioner in the digital economy, clean energy and the development of SMEs, but has also accumulated rich experience in these fields, noting that China is now translating its development experience into concrete actions to promote common regional development. SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, calling for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the Asia-Pacific miracle. Experts said Xi's speech at the gathering outlined China's vision for a stronger, more integrated Asia-Pacific community, offering a roadmap for the region to build on the achievements of the past three decades. They also said it could help deepen regional cooperation, create new opportunities for shared development and contribute to peace, stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific and beyond. A SHARED VISION In his Thursday speech, Xi stressed that building an Asia-Pacific community requires solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. These requirements are interconnected and mutually reinforcing, said Herbert Sima, director of the China Studies Center at the University of Auckland, noting they not only provide guidance for economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, but also offer valuable insights into addressing global uncertainties. Solidarity and mutual assistance form the foundation of cooperation, openness and connectivity provide a pathway for development, innovation and progress serve as the driving force for growth, while inclusive development is key to ensuring that cooperation is sustainable and benefits all parties, the expert explained. In his speech, Xi reviewed the achievements of the Asia-Pacific miracle over the past thirty-plus years, stressing the need to adapt to the new realities, take new strides and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation in the face of new opportunities and challenges. Xi's remarks have prompted experts to again reflect on the factors behind the region's remarkable economic growth and the prospects for its future development. Virdika Rizky Utama, executive director of the Jakarta-based think tank PARA Syndicate, said the Asia-Pacific miracle had been driven by open cooperation, trade and investment, and the integration of regional industrial and supply chains. What Xi stressed about building the Asia-Pacific community offered a response to the challenges facing the region and a vision for future cooperation, he said. The expert particularly noted Xi's mention of "open regionalism" in his speech, saying that for developing economies such as Indonesia, the concept means access to broader markets and more convenient connectivity. Tran Thi Hai Yen, a researcher at the Institute for European and Americas Studies at Vietnam Academy of Social Sciences, said Xi's vision comes at a timely moment, which addresses the four practical needs currently facing the Asia-Pacific region. As the rotating chair of APEC this year, she added, China has further clarified the direction of cooperation and underscored the urgency of accelerating joint efforts, helping translate long-term vision into concrete cooperation agendas. History proves that economies can prosper through trade with one another, and Xi reaffirmed the value of trade cooperation and open regionalism, said Craig Emerson, director of the Australia APEC Study Center. Such remarks are highly encouraging at a time when trade liberalization has faced growing skepticism in recent years, noted Emerson, a former Australian trade minister. "If the Asia-Pacific miracle of the past more than three decades was a story of economic growth achieved through openness and cooperation, the next 30 years should be a story of shared prosperity achieved through inclusiveness and win-win cooperation," said South Korean lawmaker Kim Tae-nyeon. "Economies in the Asia-Pacific region differ in terms of economic size, stages of development, history and culture, making the region highly diverse," he said. "This diversity should be regarded as a valuable resource. We should leverage our respective strengths, complement one another's weaknesses and turn these differences into new opportunities for cooperation." BUILDING PILLARS TOGETHER China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, and it is ready to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community, Xi said in his speech. He also called for strengthening the pillar of economy and trade, upgrading the pillar of connectivity, fostering the pillar of innovation and enhancing the pillar of development. On the importance of connectivity, Alvaro Echeverria, director of the Asia Pacific Chamber of Commerce in Chile, said the call to upgrade the pillar of connectivity was particularly relevant in the current international environment. Greater proximity helps create mutual understanding, Echeverria told Xinhua, saying he welcomes China's call to strengthen connectivity not only through physical infrastructure, but also through continued efforts to promote human development and closer people-to-people exchanges. These efforts could help rebuild trust at a time when the world faces considerable uncertainty and a lack of predictability, while the need for international coordination continues to grow, he added. Xi pointed out that China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, and announced that China will provide 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC's practical cooperation, and to establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges and provide intellectual support. In addition, Xi said that in line with the needs of Asia-Pacific cooperation, China will set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy, and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to contribute to innovation-driven and green growth in the Asia-Pacific. China's proposal to set up cooperation institutions focusing on the digital economy, clean energy and SME cooperation carries great significance and represents a key step in fostering new growth drivers for the Asia-Pacific, said Vitaly Mankevich, president of the Russian-Asian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs. "As a recognized technology leader in the digital economy, clean energy and related sectors, China can use these cooperation bodies to advance pragmatic cooperation among Asia-Pacific economies and build science and technology innovation partnerships," Mankevich said. Georgie Too Hann Huei, COO of the Malaysia-China Business Council in Kuala Lumpur, said China is not only an active practitioner in the digital economy, clean energy and the development of SMEs, but has also accumulated rich experience in these fields, noting that China is now translating its development experience into concrete actions to promote common regional development. "This approach of 'getting its own house in order first and then bringing partners along' demonstrates China's leading role and exemplary influence in regional cooperation," he said. ■

item.title: Xi, Prabowo announce launch of China-Indonesia comprehensive economic partnership negotiations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Prabowo is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Friday announced the launch of negotiations for a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership. The announcement was made during Xi's meeting with Prabowo in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Prabowo is in China for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. Xi said the two countries should strengthen strategic communication and solidarity, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, consolidate the foundation of political trust, and jointly guard against and respond to external risks. He called on both countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and clean energy. Xi called for efforts to reach an all-round, high-standard comprehensive economic partnership agreement at an early date. Amid emerging risks and challenges in the world, China is ready to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Indonesia within multilateral frameworks, including the United Nations, APEC and China-ASEAN cooperation, Xi said. Prabowo said Indonesia's strategic partnership with China is stronger than ever, reaffirming that Indonesia firmly adheres to the one-China policy and that Taiwan is a province of the People's Republic of China. Indonesia sincerely welcomes Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in the country, and is committed to providing a reliable, stable and predictable business environment, Prabowo said. Prabowo said Indonesia highly appreciates China's role as a responsible major country in international affairs, and stands ready to work with China to safeguard the shared interests of the Global South and promote regional and global peace and stability. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Prabowo is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong)

item.title: Xi says China, Australia should be mutually trusted partners
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Albanese is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Friday that China and Australia should be cooperative partners who trust each other and help each other succeed, as the two countries have no historical grievances or conflicts of fundamental interests. China-Australia relations are stable at present, said Xi when meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Albanese is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. As next year marks the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Australia, Xi called on the two sides to achieve greater progress in bilateral relations from a new starting point. Xi said that in a volatile and turbulent world, the two countries should enhance mutual trust, accommodate each other's core interests and major concerns, and keep to the right direction of friendship and cooperation. He called for deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in pursuit of the two countries' respective development goals, advancing traditional cooperation in agriculture, energy and minerals, and expanding cooperation in emerging areas such as the green economy, new energy, the digital industry, artificial intelligence (AI) and climate change response. Efforts should be made to promote friendship between the two countries through expanded people-to-people exchanges, Xi said, noting that the two sides had agreed to designate 2027 as the China-Australia Year of Tourism. He also emphasized the need to strengthen multilateral coordination in addressing global challenges, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community, and jointly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law. Albanese said that the improvement and development of Australia-China relations serves the interests of both sides and brings tangible benefits to the peoples of both countries. He said that Australia stands ready to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen practical cooperation in trade, investment, AI and other areas, deepen people-to-people exchanges, respect each other and properly handle differences, so as to make Australia-China relations an example for countries with different systems to develop constructive relations. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Albanese is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong)
